paper.title_en: Measurement of the $^{169}$Tm$(γ,n)$$^{168}$Tm Cross Section and Implications for $γ$-Process Calculations
paper.abstract_en: The $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(γ,n)^{168}\mathrm{Tm}$ cross section has been measured at the Shanghai Laser Electron Gamma Source (SLEGS) using quasi-monoenergetic laser-Compton-scattering $γ$ rays over the energy range from the neutron threshold to 14.61~MeV. The photon flux and energy distribution were determined with a LaBr$3$(Ce) spectrometer, and monoenergetic cross sections were obtained using an iterative unfolding method. Below 12~MeV, the present cross sections agree well with the NewSUBARU data and the IAEA-2019 evaluations. However, near the maximum of the $(γ,n)$ excitation function, the present cross sections are significantly higher than both the NewSUBARU data and the IAEA-2019 evaluated values. The $E1$$γ$-ray strength functions were derived by fitting the experimental cross sections measured at SLEGS and NewSUBARU. The stellar reaction rates for $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(γ,n)$ and $^{168}\mathrm{Tm}(n,γ)$ were calculated by incorporating these constrained $γ$-ray strength functions into the TALYS code. The calculated $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(γ,n)$ rates were adopted in a full $p$-process reaction network for the shock-heated O/Ne-rich layers of a $20 M\odot$ core-collapse supernova model to perform a sensitivity analysis. The updated rates have a negligible effect on the final $p$-nucleus abundances.
